subject: Oceanography
title: Spring and Neap Tides
description: A fast breakdown of Spring and Neap Tides for builders.

hook.text: Twice a month, tides surge higher and drain lower than usual—and twice a month, they barely move.

buildup.text: Spring tides occur at new and full moons—when the Sun, Moon, and Earth align.

discovery.text: Their gravitational pulls add up, producing extra-high high tides and extra-low low tides.

twist.text: Neap tides occur at quarter moons—Sun and Moon pull at right angles, partially canceling each other.

climax.text: The tidal range during springs can be double that of neaps—critical for navigation and coastal life.

punchline.text: The Moon and Sun team up or compete—twice each month.

quiz.question: When do spring tides occur?
options: At new and full moons when Sun and Moon align
